# Marky v1.7.0

Saving is no longer something you have to remember to do. Notes are written
automatically a couple of seconds after you stop typing, and on every way out of
one: switching notes, closing a tab, leaving the window, closing the window, or
quitting the app.

### Automatic saving

- **Writes happen in the background.** Two seconds after your last keystroke,
  the note is on disk. No save shortcut to press, no prompt on close, and
  nothing left in memory when you walk away.
- **Flushed on every exit.** Switching notes or closing a tab immediately writes
  any pending changes so other tools or git see the latest edit instantly.
- **Quitting holds for the flush.** Quitting via Cmd/Ctrl+Q or the app menu
  briefly holds exit until any active note has flushed to disk, so you never lose
  the last sentence typed before quitting.
- **Detached windows included.** Notes opened in their own window get the same
  background saving, blur flushing, and graceful exit handling.
- **Scratch buffers become real files.** Typing into a new scratch note when a
  vault is open automatically saves it as a note on first keystroke.
- **Manual mode is still there.** If you prefer explicit Cmd/Ctrl+S saving,
  manual mode with dirty markers and save-on-close confirmation can be enabled
  in Settings → Editor.

### Under the hood

- **Silent self-writes.** Marky now tags its own file writes so the file
  watcher drops the echo, eliminating the "Scanning folder..." reload spinner
  that previously triggered on every save.
- **Smart history snapshots.** Snapshot history is now throttled to one per note
  every three minutes (with forced snapshots on major boundaries), keeping
  undo history meaningful instead of filling up with two-second autosaves.
- **Streamlined conflict handling.** The redundant external conflict modal has
  been removed in favor of direct editor state preservation.
